title: The Hunchback of Notre Dame
tagline: Ring the bells. Ring the dinner bell.
about: A kind bell-ringer hidden in Notre Dame sneaks out to the Festival of Fools in Paris.

Notre Dame Bell TowerThe Hunchback of Notre DameRing the bells. Ring the dinner bell.Every recipe serves 4.

    To beginHam and gruyere crêpesThin crêpes folded around ham and melted gruyereHow to make it150g plain flour2 eggs375ml milk30g butter, for the pan150g leg ham150g gruyere, grated2 tbsp caster sugar1 lemonWhisk the flour, eggs and milk into a smooth batter.Rest the batter.Cook thin crepes in a pan, brushing it with the butter between each one.Fill half with ham and gruyere, fold and warm until melted.Sprinkle the rest with sugar and lemon juice and fold into quarters.Brie, fig jam and tomato crostiniHugo, Victor and Laverne say go to the festival. Brie and fig, tomato and basil.How to make it1 baguette2 tbsp olive oil150g brie2 tbsp fig jam3 tomatoes1/4 cup basil leavessalt, to tasteSlice the baguette and brush with oil.Toast the slices until golden.Top half with brie and fig jam.Top the rest with chopped tomato, torn basil and salt.From the hearthBell tower beef and mushroom braiseBeef, bacon and mushroom braise. You're not eating, boy.How to make it150g bacon, diced1.2kg beef chuck, diced2 tbsp olive oil12 baby onions, peeled300g mushrooms2 tbsp plain flour2 tbsp tomato paste750ml beef stock1 tbsp red wine vinegar4 sprigs of thyme2 bay leaves1kg potatoes60g butter100ml milkDice the bacon and beef and peel the baby onions.Brown the bacon in the oil, then the beef in batches.Add the onions and mushrooms and colour lightly.Stir in the flour and tomato paste, then add the stock, vinegar, thyme and bay leaves.Cover and simmer gently until the beef is tender.Peel and boil the potatoes, then mash with butter and warm milk.Serve the braise over the mash.Clopin's garlic and olive chickenClopin tells the story with his puppets. Olive and lemon chicken, crusty bread.How to make itNot on tonight's cookChicken thighs braised with garlic, green olives, lemon and herbs until tender and saucy, with crusty bread to mop it all up.Season 1kg chicken thighs and brown skin side down in olive oil for 6 minutes, then turn.Add 10 whole peeled garlic cloves, 100g green olives, 1 sliced lemon, thyme and 2 bay leaves.Pour in 300ml chicken stock, cover and simmer gently for 30 minutes, then uncover and bubble for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens.Scatter with parsley and serve with crusty bread.Sweet thingsKing of Fools madeleinesCrowned King of Fools at the festival. Lemon butter shells.How to make it100g butter2 eggs100g caster sugar1 lemon, zested100g plain flour2 tbsp icing sugarMelt the butter and cool.Whisk the eggs, sugar and lemon zest until thick.Fold in the flour and butter.Rest the batter.Spoon into greased shell tins.Bake at 200°C until puffed and golden.Dust with icing sugar.Mugs and cupsDjali's grenadine lime sirop sodaHomemade pomegranate syrup and lime over ice, topped with sodaHow to make it250ml pomegranate juice100g caster sugar1 lemon1 lime1 L soda water4 cups iceSimmer the pomegranate juice and sugar until slightly syrupy, then add a squeeze of lemon.Cool the grenadine.Fill tall glasses with ice and add lime juice to each.Top with soda water, then slowly pour the grenadine down the side of each glass so it settles at the bottom. Serve with a spoon.
